evidence_summary: Fuzzboxes documents Universal Amplifier Corp. as the manufacturer, gives the 615 West 131st Street New York address from Astro Amp literature, and uses dated surviving examples to place production from 1967 through 1969. This is the anchor product for the Universal Amplifier dirt branch.

Fuzzboxes documents early Sam Ash Fuzzz Boxx units with the same PCB and component mixture as the earliest Astrotone and later dated Sam Ash examples with the same evolving production states. Sam Ash's historical account also identifies Universal Amplifier as the manufacturer.

Fuzzboxes lists the Fuzz-Stainer as a later Sam Ash fuzz after Fuzzz Boxx production ended, but does not identify Universal Amplifier as its builder. It must not inherit the Astrotone factory relationship from branding alone.

Fuzzboxes explicitly identifies Sam Ash Fuzzola pedals as initially built by Shin-Ei in Japan and later by JEN in Italy. This is a separate supply chain from Universal Amplifier and demonstrates that Sam Ash used multiple external builders across its fuzz catalog.

Hewitt's Garage Studio identifies the JEN Jumbo Fuzz as the same family sold as Dallas-Arbiter Jumbo Fuzz, Sam Ash Jumbo Fuzz and Sam Ash Fuzzola II, with an estimated 1973-1975 period. It is separate from the Universal Amplifier Astrotone branch.

Independent historical references consistently identify Astro Amp / Universal Amplifier Corp. as the New York maker of the Astrotone. No additional independently verified OEM dirt model attributable to Universal Amplifier was found in this pass beyond Sam Ash Fuzzz Boxx.

Current source review did not produce a defensible third vintage dirt pedal identity that can be promoted into the Universal Amplifier production branch. The archive should therefore resist expanding the factory's OEM list from generic New York manufacture claims or visual similarity alone.
